K-fold cross-validation for mvgam fits

Source: R/kfold.mvgam.R
kfold.mvgam.Rd

Estimates the expected log predictive density of held-out groups of rows. A fold that importance sampling approximates well takes the PSIS estimate of loo::loo() on the fold's summed log likelihood. The rest are refitted without the fold, as lfo_cv.mvgam() refits the time blocks it cannot approximate. Three settings cover the range:

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
kfold(
  x,
  K = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  folds = NULL,
  exact = FALSE,
  pareto_k_threshold = NULL,
  fold_split = c("grouped", "stratified", "random"),
  seed = NULL,
  silent = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fitted mvgam object.

K

Integer number of folds. With group and K = NULL (the default), each group is a fold. A K below the number of groups bins the groups into K folds with loo::kfold_split_grouped(). Without group, K defaults to 10.

group

Optional character vector of training-data columns whose combinations define the groups. NULL (the default) takes the closure unit of an occ() or nmix() model and the row otherwise.

folds

Optional integer vector of one fold per training row, replacing K and fold_split. Each fold is then held out and scored as one group. A fold never splits a group, which is a closure unit by default.

exact

Logical. TRUE refits every fold. Defaults to FALSE.

pareto_k_threshold

Numeric. A fold whose Pareto-k exceeds it is refitted. NULL (the default) takes min(1 - 1 / log10(S), 0.7) for S posterior draws. Inf refits nothing.

fold_split

"grouped" (the default), "stratified" or "random": the loo::kfold_split_*() function binning groups into K folds when there are more groups than folds.

seed

Optional integer seed for the fold split and the refits. The session's random state is restored when the call returns.

silent

Integer in \{0, 1, 2\}. 0 prints each refit and its sampler start and finish lines. 1 (default) prints the refit count. 2 prints nothing.

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

Value

A c("mvgam_kfold", "kfold", "loo") object, which loo::loo_compare() takes as it takes loo.mvgam() results. It holds:

  • estimates: elpd_kfold, p_kfold and kfoldic with their standard errors.

  • pointwise: the ELPD of each group. pointwise_psis holds the PSIS estimates before any refit.

  • pareto_k: the Pareto-k of each group's PSIS estimate, all NA under exact = TRUE.

  • n_refits and refit_groups: the number of refitted folds and the groups they hold.

  • K and exact: the number of folds and the mode.

  • group: the grouping columns, "fold" when folds was given, or NULL for single rows.

  • pareto_k_threshold: the threshold applied, with pareto_k_threshold_adaptive TRUE when the default rule set it.

Details

  • pareto_k_threshold = Inf refits nothing. Pareto-k warnings mark folds the approximation fits poorly.

  • The default refits the folds whose Pareto-k exceeds pareto_k_threshold, which is often a handful.

  • exact = TRUE refits every fold, as brms::kfold() does.

group takes several columns, such as c("site", "season"). Every row of one combination stays in the same fold.

References

Burkner P-C, Gabry J, Vehtari A (2020). Approximate leave-future-out cross-validation for Bayesian time series models. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation, 90(14), 2499–2523. doi:10.1080/00949655.2020.1783262 .

Vehtari A, Gelman A, Gabry J (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing, 27, 1413–1432. doi:10.1007/s11222-016-9696-4 .

See also

loo.mvgam() approximates leave-one-out cross-validation. lfo_cv.mvgam() scores forecasts from rolling origins. summary.mvgam_kfold() and plot.mvgam_kfold() report each group. The forecast evaluation article compares models by cross-validation.

Other model comparison: bridge_sampler.mvgam(), compare_elpds(), lfo_cv.mvgam(), log_lik.mvgam(), loo.mvgam(), loo_compare.mvgam_lfo(), mvgam_loo_extras, posterior_average.mvgam(), waic.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = gaussian(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, type = 6L)

mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(season, bs = "cc"),
              trend_formula = ~ CAR(),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = gaussian(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 3 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# Neighbouring times share information through the trend. Folds of
# contiguous time blocks hold each block out whole. Folds that PSIS
# approximates poorly are refitted.
blocks <- cut(simdat$data_train$time, breaks = 4L, labels = FALSE)
k <- kfold(mod, folds = blocks)
#> kfold: refitting 4 fold(s) ...
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 1 of 2 chains had an E-BFMI less than 0.3.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 6 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 5 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 23 of 2000 (1.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
k
#> mvgam k-fold cross-validation
#>   elpd_kfold : -135.79 (SE 10.72)
#>   kfoldic    : 271.58 (SE 21.43)
#>   groups     : 4 (fold)
#>   refits     : 4 of 4 folds
#>   Pareto k   : max 1.62, median 1.31, threshold 0.70 (adaptive)
#> 
#> Lowest ELPD (share of the total):
#>   2                    -41.30 (30.4%)
#>   1                    -34.51 (25.4%)
#>   4                    -30.49 (22.5%)
#> 
#> Largest change from PSIS to refit:
#>   2                    -34.82 -> -41.30
#>   1                    -31.30 -> -34.51
#>   3                    -27.84 -> -29.49

# The ELPD and Pareto k of each block
plot(k)
